E1.evidence: Labelled bug with reproducer: "1. Make a hardware with a JS broadcaster and an FTS broadcaster. 2. Load both controllers 3. configure the JS broadcaster 4. controller_manager will die" -- https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1164 ; maintainer confirmation: "Thank you for reporting the issue. I've addressed the above bug in the linked PR." -- https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1164#issuecomment-1808709963

E2.evidence: Plugin (force_torque_sensor_broadcaster, ros2_controllers) and host framework (controller_manager, ros2_control) are separate units. The failure depends on a documented call-order assumption across that boundary: controller_interface_base.hpp states "The method is called only in `inactive` or `active` state, i.e., `on_configure` has to be called first." for both command_interface_configuration() and state_interface_configuration(), while the host's controller_sorting calls `ctrl_a.c->command_interface_configuration().names` and `ctrl_a.c->state_interface_configuration().names` on every loaded controller (controller_manager.cpp at humble b9cdcfe0). The plugin relies on that precondition: its state_interface_configuration() returns `force_torque_sensor_->get_state_interface_names()` where `force_torque_sensor_` is created only in on_configure. Not deployment wiring or build: the fix changes the host's calls (PR 1165).

E3.evidence: PAIR: the host consumes the plugin's interface-configuration output while sorting ("the controller sorting in configuring the other controller will also check the FTS broadcasterf for sorting. For this it will try to fetch all state and command interfaces" -- https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1164).

E4.evidence: Observed crash: "4. controller_manager will die" and "First of all I would expect things not to crash." -- https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1164

failed_conditions.quote: However that can lead to situations where when the FTS broadcaster is loaded but not yet configured and another controller is configured the controller sorting in configuring the other controller will also check the FTS broadcasterf for sorting. For this it will try to fetch all state and command interfaces which will use the [`force_torque_sensor_` object](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/232154dab5f5363704c7f7640b2d42f5d6f3665b/force_torque_sensor_broadcaster/src/force_torque_sensor_broadcaster.cpp#L124) which unfortunately is a nullpointer before the FTS broadcaster has been configured.

loudness_evidence: The source reports the process dying ("4. controller_manager will die" -- https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1164) with no diagnostic from existing tooling (no load/claim/activation error is emitted before the crash).

resolution.evidence: No change resolving the failure was merged or tested; the thread ends without a fix.

notes: Canonical api forms: element names use the controller_interface base-class symbols through which controller_manager calls the plugin; command_interface_configuration, state_interface_configuration, is_chainable and update are pure virtuals implemented by the plugin, while init, configure, get_state, assign_interfaces, release_interfaces and get_node are implemented in the controller_interface library (ros2_control) and inherited by the plugin object, which is why the plugin is listed as providing them. The failed-condition class is `other` because the mismatch is a lifecycle call-order precondition (the documented statement "The method is called only in `inactive` or `active` state, i.e., `on_configure` has to be called first."), which no listed class covers. The plugin's command_interface_configuration() returns NONE without touching `force_torque_sensor_`, so the crash itself comes from state_interface_configuration(); both calls violate the same documented precondition. Possible UPGRADE framing (not recorded as the operation because the source does not state it): controller sorting was newly backported to humble in d143a4f2 (#1157, 2023-11-07) six days before the report, and the reporter asked for the fix before "the Humble sync", while the plugin was unchanged. The reporter's alternative fix (read the interface parameters in on_init in the plugin) was not the adopted resolution. Commits a8782f0c44134124298ca56f2fb1e31a2db719f6 and d63048dbe0996ad66f7c7135bf8417d4fd0a8a0e are cherry-picks of 75e7efd1 with parents b9cdcfe0 (humble) and 0bcd9faa (iron), i.e. the backport branch heads; the packet's peterdavidfagan fork URL points to the same master commit 75e7efd1. The reporter notes the problem is probably also present on Iron and Rolling but tested only Humble.
